correctness.rationale: Each binary parity pattern \(b\) has exactly \(2^{p-\operatorname{wt}(b)}\) ternary lifts. The syndrome parity identity \(\sigma(b)\equiv\operatorname{wt}(b)\pmod2\) is correct. Under cyclic right rotation, the syndrome changes modulo \(p\) by the cyclic transition count; for a nonconstant word this is a positive even integer below the odd prime \(p\), so every nonconstant orbit has size \(p\) and its syndromes modulo \(p\) are equidistributed. Summing ordinary and signed lift weights gives the stated \(T_r\) and \(D_r\), and the opposite parities of the two residues above each class modulo \(p\) give all four formulas. Independent exhaustive binary checks at \(p=3,5,7,11\) reproduced them and the minimizer set; finite covering checks are not used to prove the all-prime cardinality law. The covering property itself follows directly from the source theorem because \(\lfloor3/2\rfloor=1\).

evidence: The exact direct q-ary DVT size formulas weight q-ary differential words uniformly; the ternary parity lift weights a binary parity pattern by \(2^{p-\operatorname{wt}(b)}\).
